lines.ov1: Cells burn glucose with oxygen to release energy, and store it as A T P.
lines.gly1: In the cytoplasm, glycolysis splits glucose into two pyruvate.
lines.gly2: It nets two A T P, and needs no oxygen.
lines.kr1: Inside the mitochondrion, pyruvate is broken down by the Krebs cycle.
lines.kr2: Carbon leaves as carbon dioxide, and carriers pick up high energy electrons.
lines.et1: Electrons pass along the electron transport chain, pumping protons across a membrane.
lines.et2: Protons flow back through A T P synthase, making most of the A T P, while oxygen takes the electrons and forms water.
lines.tal1: One glucose yields about thirty A T P, roughly fifteen times more than without oxygen.
lines.outro: Glucose and oxygen in. Carbon dioxide, water, and energy out. That is cellular respiration.
